title: Philosophy workflow: reconstruction without authority leakage
audience: Readers with no prior knowledge of Chalxius or knowledge graphs

source_snapshot.description: An anonymized public summary bound to a read-only audit of a private philosophy workflow.

presentation.subtitle: Two workflow conclusions, with research and learning context available as optional layers.
presentation.introduction: This interactive map demonstrates separation of source, interpretation, audit, exploration, and learning authority. It does not prove a philosophical conclusion and admits no Fact.

audit.summary: The audited artifact passed current read-only structural and workflow checks; that result is workflow evidence only.
warnings: The underlying artifact predates current unified-write activation and remains read-only.

themes.label: Philosophy workflow
themes.description: A source-bound reconstruction followed by an authority-separation result.

nodes.title: Frozen source anchors
nodes.summary: Exact source passages remain separate from every interpretation.
nodes.intuition: The system first preserves what the publication says before asking what it means.
nodes.importance: A later criticism can then point to a stable source instead of a moving paraphrase.
nodes.reasoning: Source authority is evidence of wording and context, not automatic proof of the paper's conclusion.

nodes.title: Bounded argument map
nodes.summary: A reconstruction makes claims and inferential links explicit while remaining interpretation.
nodes.intuition: It is a transparent reading of the paper, not a silent replacement for the paper.
nodes.importance: Typed reconstruction makes omissions, ambiguities, and disagreements inspectable.
nodes.reasoning: The audited snapshot contained 40 reconstruction nodes and retained rejected revisions as history.

nodes.title: Independent dual review
nodes.summary: The accepted revision required separate source-fidelity and graph-structure review.
nodes.intuition: One reviewer checks faithfulness to the source; another checks whether the map itself is coherent.
nodes.importance: A polished reconstruction cannot approve itself.
nodes.reasoning: The two reviews bind different failure modes and preserve their decisions independently.

nodes.title: Correctable audit history
nodes.summary: Rejected, superseded, and repaired audit states remain inspectable.
nodes.intuition: Correction adds a traceable next state instead of erasing the earlier mistake.
nodes.importance: Readers can distinguish the current view from the path that produced it.
nodes.reasoning: Append-only replacement prevents a later repair from rewriting the historical record.

nodes.title: Source-bound reconstruction
nodes.summary: Chalxius can make a philosophical argument readable without merging source and interpretation.
nodes.intuition: A reader can inspect the argument and still see which parts came from the publication and which parts were reconstructed.
nodes.importance: This supports rigorous reading without pretending that a graph settles the philosophy.
nodes.reasoning: Frozen source anchors, explicit reconstruction, and independent review jointly support this workflow claim.

nodes.title: Zero admitted Facts
nodes.summary: The audited Fact Graph contained zero admitted Facts and zero candidates.
nodes.intuition: Useful analysis can remain useful without being promoted into trusted premises.
nodes.importance: This is positive evidence that authority did not leak between planes.
nodes.reasoning: A clean workflow audit checks structure and policy; it does not certify a philosophical proposition.

nodes.title: Authority-safe exploration
nodes.summary: Audit, exploration, teaching, and presentation remain nontruth activities unless a separate admission succeeds.
nodes.intuition: The system can help people think without granting every useful note the power of a premise.
nodes.importance: That boundary is the central safety property of the philosophy workflow.
nodes.reasoning: The read-only audit passed while the Fact Graph remained empty and the learning mount prohibited writeback.

nodes.intuition: Researchers can try objections without editing the source or declaring victory.
nodes.reasoning: Mirror nodes retain bindings to their source snapshots while agent notes remain exploration only.

nodes.title: Read-only learning overlay
nodes.summary: A learning overlay can teach from frozen research snapshots without writing back.
nodes.intuition: Teaching state is about what a learner has practiced, not what research has proved.
nodes.importance: Pedagogical usefulness does not weaken provenance or admission boundaries.
nodes.reasoning: The verified mount prohibited research-runtime invocation, truth inheritance, and source writeback.
